text:
Jordan (CS): Customer (AcmeAnalytics) just reported structured output failures after last night's canary. They say our JSON schema validator started failing on multiple endpoints. Escalating — they want immediate help.

Alex W: Can you paste a repro (curl + request payload) and a couple of raw model responses? Also which model id/version did the customer get routed to?

Jordan (CS): Repro from customer (redacted):
```bash
curl -s -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood/llm-instruct-1.4","input":"Generate a JSON list of users with fields id,name,email,active (true/false)"}'
```
They included two sample responses they saved: one that used to pass, and one that failed validation.

Failed response (raw):
```json
{"status":"ok","users": null}
```
(validator error: `users` must be array of objects)

Another failing variant they saw sometimes (random):
```json
{"status":"ok","users":[{"id":1,"name":"A. Brown","email":"a@x.com","active":true},],}
```
(trailing comma, extra comma before closing array/object)

Alex W: Yikes. That looks like the model returning text that includes trailing commas or `null` when it should be empty array. Two questions: 1) Was this customer pinned to the v1.3 model previously? 2) Did we change any system prompt or format instruction for the 1.4 rollout?

Jordan (CS): They were on the default routing (not pinned). We rolled 1.4 canary to 20% on 2025-11-02, then bumped to 75% at ~03:20 UTC last night as part of automated ramp. Customer said failures started ~03:45 UTC and spiked through the morning.

SRE Bot: metric spike: `schema_validation_failures.customer.acmeanalytics` +160x between 03:40-04:30 UTC. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/metrics/abc123 :eyes:

Maria T: tagging @eng-runtime — can you confirm if any pre/post-processing (json sanitizers) were toggled during that deploy? Also, was quantization/fastpath changed for the 1.4 compiled kernels?

Alex W: I tried a repro locally against the same model id and got intermittently bad outputs. Here's a trimmed run (3 attempts):

Attempt 1 (OK):
```json
{"status":"ok","users":[{"id":1,"name":"A. Brown","email":"a@x.com","active":true}]}
```
Attempt 2 (BAD):
```json
{"status":"ok","users": null}
```
Attempt 3 (BAD formatting):
```json
{"status":"ok","users":[{"id":1,"name":"A. Brown","email":"a@x.com","active":true},],}
```

Alex W: So it's non-deterministic but reproducible for me at ~30% of tries.

Maria T: Two hypotheses: 1) The updated system prompt for 1.4 accidentally softened the instruction to emit strict JSON (maybe an extra newline or humanizing prefix); 2) a new kernel/beam changes tokenization leading to trailing punctuation. I'll pull the 1.4 rollout changelog and compare system prompts.

Chris P: From ML side, we sometimes see generation of punctuation artifacts when a model was fine-tuned with examples that include trailing commas or conversational framing. If 1.4 included additional in-context examples for "human-friendly lists", that could explain trailing commas / `null` fallbacks. We should diff the finetune dataset.

Emily R: Customer is Enterprise and on a monthly SLA. They asked for rollback to the previous stable model and an incident update. I propose: 1) Pin their requests to 1.3 for now (customer-specific override), 2) Pause further ramp of 1.4, 3) Full rollback for default routing until root cause found. Can eng-runtime action pin/rollback?

Maria T: I can pin that customer to 1.3 (routing rule) — doing it now for acmeanalytics account id xxxx. Pausing global ramp — toggling canary ramp to 20% hold.

SRE Bot: routing change applied: `route(acmeanalytics) -> redwood/llm-instruct-1.3` (audited by maria.t).

Jordan (CS): Customer confirmed after pin they no longer see validation failures on their tests. They asked for ETA on root cause and fix plan.

Alex W: Quick triage notes: adding stricter post-request sanitizer on our side reduces customer-visible failures but does not fix root cause (model is still producing malformed JSON). For long term we need to update the generation prompt and possibly add deterministic decoding settings for structured-output endpoints (e.g., lower top_p, force tokens).

Maria T: I'm opening an internal bug and assigning to eng-ml + eng-runtime: BUG-2025-442: "1.4 structured output regression: trailing commas / null instead of empty array". I'll attach example requests, seed tokens, and kernel logs.

Chris P: Plan from ML: 1) Run targeted eval suite with the exact structured-output prompt set at varying temperatures and decoding params (greedy vs top-k/top-p) 2) If prompt fix insufficient, revert fine-tune examples that introduced human-friendly list formatting. 3) Add a strict-format instruction in system prompt for structured endpoints.

Emily R: Please post a short incident summary for the customer: what happened, workaround (pinned to 1.3), and our next steps. I'll send the external update after we confirm rollout plan.

Jordan (CS): Will do. Putting this thread into the incident and adding the customer-facing message draft.

Alex W: FYI for oncall — repro curl I used (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood/llm-instruct-1.4","input":"Return ONLY JSON array named users with id,name,email,active"}'
```
I also attached a small script that retries up to 5x and rejects malformed JSON. Works as a temporary mitigation for integrations.

SRE Bot: incident created: INC-2025-1187. Priority: P2.

Maria T: I'll follow up with a diff of system prompts + commit hash for 1.4 by EOD.

Chris P: I'll run the structured-output evaluation overnight and report token-level failure modes tomorrow morning.

Emily R: Thanks all. Jordan — update customer that we've pinned them and created an incident. Keep me in the loop for any SLA escalation. :white_check_mark:

Jordan (CS): Customer updated and satisfied for now. Leaving thread open for eng updates.
